title: Chicken or turkey with rice and vegetables (no carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens), no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of tender chicken or turkey meat, boiled rice, and a mix of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens. It is prepared without any sauces, making it a light and nutritious option for those monitoring fat and sugar intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are excellent sources of lean protein.
Rice provides complex carbohydrates that give sustained energy.
Skipping sauce helps keep sodium levels low.
The recipe can be easily customized by swapping different vegetables.
Cooking without frying preserves more vitamins in the vegetables.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey contain all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Steady energy supply
items.content: Rice releases glucose slowly, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of sauce and the use of lean poultry make the dish suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, or cauliflower add vitamin C, potassium, and dietary fiber.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables and rice aids gut health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or turkey, experiencing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Salt control
items.content: Even without sauce, keep added salt to a minimum to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Thorough cooking
items.content: Poultry must be fully cooked to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

items.title: Vegetable selection
items.content: Certain vegetables can cause gas in sensitive people; choose easily digestible options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish warm; garnish with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill for extra flavor. It works well in a lunch container or as the base for a nutrient‑dense bowl.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before eating.
